summary.intent: Coordinate a multi-agent effort on the caliper docgen project: land a Rust 1.99/edition 2024 upgrade, build a deterministic construct suite, spike the tsrs checker backend, run a full health check of main, and launch the next wave of work.
summary.outcome: Wave 1 produced PRs #386 (ADR), #387 (construct suite), #388 (Rust 1.99) and a tsrs spike report, all awaiting CI and approval. A health check of main was started, and wave 2 (slice 1 PropType variants, tsrs backend, construct-suite CI job) was launched as stacked branches with no results yet.

repo: Rust toolchain pins live in .prototools (read by ci.yml and weekly.yml), callisto-release.yml RUST_VERSION, workspace rust-version (read by the MSRV job) and the CONTRIBUTING table; there is no rust-toolchain.toml or Dockerfile.
rustup, mise and proto shims override RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN, so workers must put the toolchain bin dir first on PATH to use 1.99.1.
Workspace denies unsafe_code, so edition 2024's unsafe set_var forced crates/cli/tests/trycmd.rs to pass COLUMNS=80 via TestCases::env.

Edition 2024 enables let chains, which produced 49 clippy collapsible_if fixes; .rustfmt.toml now uses style_edition = "2024" and the reformat touches ~98 files, so later Rust branches should stack on #388 to avoid conflicts.
Do not run oxfmt wholesale over apps/oracle/tests: it rewrites tests/fixtures/comparator-artifact-rows.json.

Construct suite lives in apps/oracle (construct-suite.ts, construct-capture.ts, construct-suite/ fixtures named <NN>-<slug>.tsx exporting Row with Props prop p, expectations.json, goldens). Scripts: construct:capture and construct:check; the test skips if the caliper binary is absent, so a skipped run is green but covers nothing.
The construct suite has 204 rows: 95 identical, 60 spelled, 28 less precise, 16 opaque with marker, 5 wrong (all tuple rest/variadic bugs). Goldens come from the Go checker as arbiter.
Caliper's TypeInfo in crates/semantic/src/rpc.rs does not read Type.intrinsicName, so unresolved types are treated as plain any; intrinsicName 'error' vs 'any' is the only distinguishing signal.
Checker discovery only looks for node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc; using tsrs needs --tsc-path or discovery of node_modules/tsrs/bin/tsrs.
The Rust client sends createPrograms[].compilerOptions where the Node SDK sends options; both work but need a regression test.
Large components need thousands of sequential checker requests (7,565 for a Chakra component), so they cannot fit the 150 ms semanticWaitMs with either backend; batching is the lever.
tsrs memory grows over long sessions (99 MB to 293 MB over 600 edits) and only a process restart reclaims it; the existing 768 MiB max_rss_mib replacement covers this.
Chakra corpus for perf checks is at /tmp/claude-501/oracle-rerun/corpora/chakra-ui/packages/react/src because fixtures/chakra has only 3 files.

code.finding: Version allow-list; adding exact entry 0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta was the only change needed for the Rust client to work with the tsrs binary.
TypeInfo lacks an intrinsic_name: Option<String> field; adding it and treating "error" as degraded would set degradedBy for unresolved types.
Uses TestCases::env for COLUMNS=80 instead of unsafe set_var under edition 2024.

workflow: Run health checks in a pristine checkout or clean-room worktree; leaked node_modules in worker worktrees caused 28 spurious test failures.
Stack dependent branches on open PRs with --base to the parent when a parent PR does a mass reformat, to avoid conflicts; merge bottom-up.
The permission classifier denied cargo build of an external git dependency ("Code from External"); the worker correctly did not work around it and surfaced it for the user to run.
Subagent/teammate reports are not user approval; mutation checks (altering an expectation or fixture) are useful to prove a test gate actually fails.
Workers that only mentally checked fixtures produced some invalid ones; an integrator pass type-checking all fixtures in one program caught them.

friction: Permission classifier blocked the in-process tsrs build, leaving compile time, binary size and in-process latency unmeasured.
rust-objcopy warns it cannot find libLLVM.dylib in the 1.99.1 install on release builds (harmless).
Worker worktrees lacking node_modules caused environment-only test failures.
feat/construct-suite branch name was held by another worktree, forcing the integrator to push through a local construct-int branch.
Construct-suite authors never ran tsc, so two rows had to be deleted after integration.
Root tsc -p tsconfig.json has 42 pre-existing errors in other packages and fixtures.
open_items: Approvals needed for PRs #388, #387, #386 and #291; CI on #388 and #387 was still running.
CI does not yet run the construct suite; the ci/construct-suite worker is adding it and making a missing binary a failure.
just msrv not verified locally (needs rustup toolchain named 1.99); CI MSRV job is the real check.
In-process tsrs linking undecided; driver ready at /tmp/claude-501/spike/inproc but build needs user approval. Likely recommendation is to stay out-of-process.
ADR 0026 cites an '87 fixtures matched' figure with no file behind it.
Batching of checker requests should be measured as the lever for the 150 ms window; Slice 4 latency gate needs rethinking.
Not verified: tsrs on Linux/Windows, NAPI addon end to end, handshake timeout and oversized-frame handling, other 17 fixtures; TS package tests beyond two integration suites.
Slice 1 PropType variants, tsrs backend swap, and construct-suite CI job were launched and results are pending; the health check of main is also pending.
Changeset in #388 is a judgment call and may be dropped; leftover worktrees /tmp/claude-501/rust199/main, rust199-clean and construct-suite-clean should be removed after merge.
Construct constructs skipped or uncovered: cross-file merging, module augmentation, forwardRef/memo wrappers, computed enum members, DOM-typed this.
